title: 六级篇章听力：儿童书译者与长凳试用
instruction: 听完整一节2篇短文及各段后读出的问题，依次选择最佳答案。音频中材料和问题各读一遍，卷面只印四个选项。本原创使用节内编号1—7，各段对应1—3、4—7题。播放器可回听，正式单次听辨条件未强制。
audio_introduction: Section B. You will hear two passages. After each, you will hear questions. Each recording and each question will be spoken only once. Choose the best answer from A, B, C and D.
source_form_notice: 六级形式参照2024年12月第一套转载Section B：2段、3/4共7回应、每题四选；原创采用节内编号，问题只在录音与作者区。全部自有虚构内容及本机合成试听，非原考试原声；未独立教研/听辨/学生难度或产品等值验证。

turns.speaker: R
turns.text: In this fictional account, translator Lena Moss is preparing a children's story for readers in another language. One character repeatedly uses a phrase that sounds ordinary to adults but is misunderstood by the child in the story. A literal translation preserves the adult meaning, yet in the new language it no longer allows the child's mistaken interpretation. The joke then disappears, and a later scene seems to have no cause. Lena considers replacing the phrase with a different expression that can produce a comparable misunderstanding. This is not a decision to improve the author's plot. It is an attempt to preserve a relationship between two parts of the existing story. She writes to the editor explaining what the literal wording loses and what the alternative changes. The editor asks her to check that the replacement works when spoken aloud, because the book is likely to be read to children. A sentence that looks neat on the page may not make the two meanings equally available to a listener. Lena tries several versions before selecting one. In a note for the publisher, she records the reason for the departure from the literal phrase. The note is not presented as something a child must study before enjoying the story. It is part of the working history of the translation. Lena says fidelity sometimes requires a translator to explain why matching individual words would fail to preserve the action those words perform in a particular narrative.

questions.spoken_question: What is lost in the literal translation of the phrase?
options: The number of characters in the story.
The child’s possible misunderstanding and its narrative effect.
Every adult meaning of the expression.
The publisher’s right to print the book.
questions.rationale: B新语言不能儿童误解→笑点及后场因果失；A/D无，C成人义反保留。

questions.spoken_question: Why does Lena consider another expression?
options: To add an unrelated joke to the author’s plot.
To avoid consulting the editor about changes.
To preserve the link between the misunderstanding and a later scene.
To remove the child character from the book.
questions.rationale: C保原叙事关系，A非加剧情/B她咨询/D不删人物。

questions.spoken_question: Why does the editor ask for a spoken test?
options: Children may encounter the story through being read to.
The book will contain no printed text.
The phrase must be sung rather than spoken.
questions.rationale: A常朗读，听到双义需测试；B/C/D无且非全无文字。

turns.speaker: R
turns.text: A fictional design team developed a bench for a university courtyard. In the studio, it looked comfortable and passed the team's stability checks. The first outdoor trial was less encouraging. Students used the far end as a place to leave bags, and the central seats were often empty. One designer proposed adding a notice telling people to sit in the intended places. Another asked whether the bench was communicating its possible uses clearly enough. The team watched without intervening for several afternoons. It noticed that the centre faced directly into a busy walking route, while the far end offered a little distance from passing groups. The designers then tested a different orientation. More people used the central seats, but the trial also revealed a new difficulty: the changed position partly narrowed the route used by a delivery trolley. The team did not treat the rise in seated users as permission to ignore that obstruction. It adjusted the position again and asked the courtyard staff to test the trolley route before fixing the bench permanently. The project did not produce a universal rule about where all benches should face. It showed how a technically sound object could still fit poorly into one setting, and how improving one observed use could complicate another. The team kept the failed positions in its project record so a later redesign would not repeat the same apparent solution without understanding why it had been abandoned.

questions.spoken_question: What did the first outdoor trial reveal?
options: The bench failed every stability check.
Students were prohibited from carrying bags.
The courtyard had no walking route.
The central seats were less used than the designers expected.
questions.rationale: Dcentre常空远端放包，A已通过稳定，B无禁包，C有忙路。

questions.spoken_question: What did observation suggest about the original central seats?
options: They were too close to the busy flow of pedestrians.
They had been reserved for delivery drivers.
They were hidden behind a locked gate.
They were the only part approved by staff.
questions.rationale: A正对busyroute，远端距离大；B/C/D无预留锁门/仅批准。

questions.spoken_question: Why was another adjustment needed after more students used the centre?
options: The new position made every seat unstable.
A revised position obstructed part of the trolley route.
The students requested that the bench be removed indoors.
The courtyard had permanently closed to deliveries.

questions.spoken_question: Why did the team retain records of unsuccessful positions?
options: To prove that no courtyard bench can be useful.
To hide the successful layout from later designers.
To explain rejected solutions and prevent their uncritical repetition.
To replace future trials with a single attendance count.
questions.rationale: C以后别不知原因重试假解；A/B/D反仍试综合use。
